industry: Auto dealers, repair shops and body shops
kicker: 31 agents for the dealership office, the service drive and the body shop
lede: Thirty-one small agents that read the files your DMS, shop system, estimating system, floorplan lender and manufacturer already export, and hand your office a worked list of what is missing, late, short or wrong.
packages: Contracts in transit by lender and age, finance reserve against what lenders paid, and F&I product chargebacks recomputed (3 agents)
Deal jackets, OFAC and Red Flags records on file, contracts in transit, reserve, cancellations, service contract remittances, deposits and we-owes (8 agents)
Floorplan against inventory, curtailments by week, used-car aging and pricing, reconditioning days and cost, loaners and demos (5 agents)
Schedules tied to the ledger, titles and temp tags, trade payoffs, DMV fees, sales tax by county, commissions and incentive claims (7 agents)
Warranty claims, open repair orders, margins, comebacks, flat-rate hours, policy adjustments, sublet, parts obsolescence and receiving (9 agents)
Open repair orders, margins, comebacks, technician hours, sublet invoices and parts receiving from Tekmetric, Shopmonkey or similar (6 agents)
Estimates and supplements against final invoices, supplements waiting on insurers, sublet, open repair orders and parts receiving (5 agents)
All 31 agents, mapped to your exports and set to the days, rates and pay plans your store confirms, one training session
Whole store for each rooftop, each store's exports mapped and its own settings confirmed separately
For dealership accounting firms, 20 groups and fixed-ops consultants serving many stores: all 31 agents, one shared setup, every store's exports mapped with its own settings
support: Support after setup: $250 a month for one pack, $600 a month for the whole store, $300 a month per rooftop for dealer groups and partner rollouts. Includes export changes, settings updates when your lender, manufacturer or state rules change, new versions and a monthly check-in.
notes: Reads the files you export; it does not log in to your DMS, shop system, estimating system, lender portal, manufacturer portal, DMV or bank.
Days, rates, pay plans, tax rates, curtailment schedules and program limits are settings your store confirms; the defaults are working examples, not any lender's, manufacturer's or state's rules.

Column layouts for CDK, Reynolds and Reynolds, Dealertrack, DealerSocket, Tekion, Tekmetric, Shopmonkey, CCC and Mitchell were written from knowledge of those exports and have not been checked against a live account; setup confirms them with your files.
The OFAC and Red Flags agent checks that records exist and are dated before delivery; it makes no compliance determination and never reads or clears a check result.
Not legal, tax, lending or accounting advice. A person decides what to claim, pay, fund, title, charge back or post.
warn: Everything runs on your computer on files you choose. Results the AI model sees have customer names, phones, e-mails, addresses and ID numbers masked. Nothing is ever paid, funded, titled, filed, sent or posted by an agent: drafts and payment lists wait for one named person's click, even in Auto mode.
groups: Every deal checked for the documents its type needs; missing and unsigned ones listed, oldest delivery first
Financed deals not yet funded, by lender and days, with open stips, short funding and money funded but not posted
Reserve each deal should earn from the buy and contract rates, against what the lender actually paid
Dealer chargebacks on cancelled service contracts, GAP and other products recomputed pro rata, and refunds not sent
Every contract sold matched to its remittance; late, short, double or missing remittances listed
OFAC and identity check records on file for each buyer and co-buyer, dated before delivery; presence only
Deposits not applied to delivered deals, due back on dead deals, or held with no deal
Promises made on deals that are late, unscheduled, or done without the cost booked
Commission per deal from your pay plans, splits and minimums, against what was paid
Inventory against the lender statement: sold and not paid off, on the statement but not in stock, balances that differ
Principal pay-downs owed under your floorplan schedule, overdue and by week ahead
Days in stock, units past your wholesale line, priced above or well below market, below cost or stale
Days and cost from acquisition to front line, units stuck with open orders or never started
Loaners and demos past or near their day and mile limits, and loaners out with no repair order
Lien payoffs not sent, sent late or short of the per diem, not cleared, or without a lien release
Title applications, trade titles, registrations and temp tags against your state's days
Rebates, dealer cash and holdback expected per unit against the manufacturer statement
Claims unpaid by age, paid short, rejected with their resubmit-by date, or debited after payment
Open orders by age and advisor; past promise, waiting on parts, warranty and internal orders open too long
Labor and parts gross by pay type and advisor; orders under your floors and parts sold below cost
The same vehicle back within your days and miles for the same work, by technician and operation
Flagged hours against clocked and punched time per technician, with jobs flagged and never worked
Goodwill with no approver, self-approved, over your review line, unexplained or repeated
Sublet lines against vendor invoices: over the PO, never invoiced, billed below cost or twice
Parts on hand by months since last sale, valued, with returnable stock first
Parts received against invoices: billed not received, received not billed, overpriced, duplicated
The latest estimate and supplements against the final invoice by labor, parts, materials and sublet
Supplements waiting on insurers, approved short or denied, with days to answer by insurer
Each schedule tied to the ledger and aged by control number; old items, credits and zero controls listed
Title and registration fees collected on each deal against what the DMV or tag agency charged
Tax on each deal recomputed from your county rate table, trade credit and caps
closing: Each one does one job, on your computer, from a file you export. It writes the list your office works from, drafts what a person may send, and never pays, funds, titles, files or posts anything itself.
